card.title: Electric Field Due to Point Charges; Field Lines

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **electric field** E = F/q₀ is the force per unit positive test charge (N/C); for a point charge $E = kq/r^2$, radially outward for positive q, inward for negative. Fields superpose as vectors: at the midpoint of two equal +2 μC charges 10 cm apart, each field is 7.2×10⁶ N/C but they cancel — net zero (NEB 2020, 3m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - E = F/q₀ = kq/r² - E_axial(dipole) = 2kp/r³; p = qd - Superposition: E = ΣEᵢ (vectors)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Test Charge Limit: The test charge $q_0$ must be infinitesimally small so it does not disturb the source charge distribution being measured.  ·  Electrostatics Only: Field lines never form closed loops only in electrostatics. With changing magnetic fields (Faraday's law), induced electric fields form closed loops.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The electric field at a point is the force per unit positive test charge placed at that point."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2024*** — 6 μC at 0.3 m: E = 6×10⁵ N/C away from the charge.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **E is force per unit positive test charge** — the test charge must be tiny to leave the field undisturbed.  ·  **At the midpoint of a like pair the fields cancel**; for an unlike pair they add.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Invisible Field Around a Charge A charge warps the space around it: any other charge placed nearby feels a force. Describing that influence as an **electric field** — force per unit positive test charge — lets us map, add and predict electric effects without touching the source.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2020, 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 Electric field and intensity **Electric field** at a point is the force experienced by a unit positive test charge placed there: $$\vec{E} = \frac{\vec{F}}{q_0} \qquad \text{unit: N/C (or V/m)}$$ - Due to a **point charge**: $E = \dfrac{kq}{r^2}$, directed radially away from a positive charge and toward a negative one.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "E = 9×10⁹ q/r² — quote direction as well as magnitude."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Two +2 μC charges 10 cm apart: E at the midpoint?** — Each field is 7.2×10⁶ N/C but they point oppositely; net E = 0 (NEB 2020).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Field-line properties are a recurring 2m — memorise four.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Field lines picture the vector field** — density = strength, tangent = direction.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: E = kq/r²; unit N/C; lines start on +, end on −, never cross.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The dipole's axial field falls as 1/r³ — faster than a single charge's 1/r² — because the two charges nearly cancel.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Point Charge Approximation: The formula $E = kq/r^2$ assumes a point charge or spherically symmetric distribution measured outside the sphere.  ·  Verified PYQs: E at 2 m from 4 μC 2023 3m; E at 0.3 m from 6 μC 2024 2m; midpoint cancellation 2020 3m; field-line properties 2024 2m; dipole moment + axial field 2024 3m.  ·  Why is the test charge imagined to be vanishingly small?
